question: What constitutes the entertainment and events sector in Uganda and how are operators categorized?
answer: The entertainment and public events sector in Uganda encompasses event promoters, event management companies, performing artistes/musicians, actors, audio/visual production studios, sound and lighting hire firms, and entertainment venues. Governed under the Income Tax Act, VAT Act, and local entertainment ordinances, operators must register with: 1) Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) for business names or limited liability company incorporation; 2) Local municipal authorities (KCCA or town councils) for public venue permits and trading licenses; 3) Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) to acquire a 10-digit TIN with obligations for Corporation Tax, Withholding Tax, PAYE, and VAT.

question: What Withholding Tax rates apply to payments made to local artistes versus foreign non-resident public entertainers?
answer: Under the Income Tax Act and the Entertainment Taxation Guide (Issue 1 Vol. 1 FY 2025-26): 1) Non-Resident Public Entertainers: A statutory 15% final Withholding Tax is imposed on gross payments made to any foreign or international artiste performing in Uganda (e.g. Sanyuka Events hiring a Congolese musician for UGX 50M must withhold 15% = UGX 7,500,000 and remit to URA); 2) Local Resident Artistes: Anyone paying a local resident artiste or performer for services rendered must withhold 6% WHT on the gross amount, irrespective of whether the payer is a gazetted withholding agent or not (e.g. hotel hiring a local musician for UGX 10M must withhold 6% = UGX 600,000); 3) Responsibility: The primary legal obligation to deduct and remit WHT within 15 days after month-end rests upon the event promoter, venue owner, or payer.

question: How does Value Added Tax (VAT) apply to concert ticket sales, public admissions, and corporate sponsorships?
answer: 1) Ticket Sales & Concert Admissions: Entertainment services are taxable supplies attracting 18% VAT; event owners with annual turnover exceeding UGX 150 million (or UGX 37.5M in 3 months) must register for VAT and account for 18% VAT included in ticket prices (Net ticket sales = Gross / 1.18; VAT = Gross - Net); 2) Gate Scrutiny: Event promoters must formally notify URA of upcoming public concerts/events in advance; URA revenue officers monitor event gates and entrances to count and scrutinize physical and digital ticket batches; 3) Corporate Sponsorship: Any sponsorship funds or in-kind sponsorship received by an events promoter requires an EFRIS VAT-inclusive fiscal invoice issued to the sponsoring corporate brand.

question: What tax obligations and equipment allowances apply to audio-visual production studios and recording houses?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/category/tax-education/entertainment/production-studios-ownership/: 1) Corporate Income Tax: 30% CIT on net chargeable profits for incorporated production studios (or presumptive turnover tax for small studios earning UGX 10M–150M); 2) Capital Allowances: Recording studios can claim accelerated depreciation on capital investments in high-tech studio gear, mixing consoles, camera apparatus, and editing suites; 3) Mandatory EFRIS: Commercial music video production, audio mastering, and broadcast editing contracts must be invoiced through EFRIS with 20-digit FDNs; 4) Royalties & Licensing: Withholding tax applies to copyright royalties and intellectual property licensing fees.

question: What tax obligations apply to event management companies coordinating staging, sound, and lighting?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/promoter-event-manager/: Event management companies handling staging, audiovisual production, lighting, and venue hire must: 1) File twice-yearly provisional corporate returns and final annual returns via Form DT-1001; 2) Withhold and remit monthly PAYE on full-time event managers and technical crew salaries by the 15th of the following month; 3) Withhold 6% WHT on subcontracted services (tent hire, sound rental, security services) exceeding UGX 1,000,000; 4) Ensure all corporate client event billing is fiscalized via EFRIS.

question: Where can I download the official URA Guide to Taxation of the Entertainment Sector?
answer: The official handbook 'A GUIDE TO TAXATION OF THE ENTERTAINMENT SECTOR' (Issue 1 Vol. 1 FY 2025-26, 20 pages) is downloadable at https://ura.go.ug/storage/2025/10/TAXATION-OF-THE-ENTERTAINMENT-SECTOR.pdf and published under URA Tax Education > Entertainment at https://ura.go.ug/en/category/tax-education/entertainment/events-companies-ownership/. Additional subsector guides include 'Overview of the Entertainment Sector' (https://ura.go.ug/en/taxation-of-public-entertainment-and-events/), 'Events Companies' (https://ura.go.ug/en/promoter-event-manager/), 'Performers and Artistes' (https://ura.go.ug/en/performers-and-artistes/), 'Production Studios' (published June 25, 2023 - 4:08 pm by Super), 'Promoters or Events Managers' (https://ura.go.ug/en/promoters-or-events-managers-faqs/), and 'Gaming, Pool betting, Casino operators and Sports betting' (https://ura.go.ug/en/gaming-poolong-casino-operators-and-sports-betting-faqs/).
